ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The first half-reaction in the image is 4H+(aq) + NO3−(aq) + 3e− → NO(g) + 2H2O(l), in which the coefficient of NO(g) is 1, and this half-reaction consumes 3 electrons. The second half-reaction is Zn(s) → Zn2+(aq) + 2e−, and this half-reaction produces 2 electrons. Reasoning: To combine into a complete oxidation-reduction reaction, the number of electrons needs to be made equal. The least common multiple of 3 and 2 is 6, so multiply the nitrate reduction half-reaction by 2, and multiply the zinc oxidation half-reaction by 3. The original coefficient of NO(g) in the nitrate reduction half-reaction is 1, and after multiplying by 2 it becomes 2. Therefore, the coefficient of NO(g) in the balanced complete reaction is 2.

method.method_draft: From the image, transcribe the two half-reactions and note the electron counts: the nitrate reduction half-reaction consumes 3e− and produces 1 NO(g), while the zinc oxidation half-reaction produces 2e−. To balance the full redox reaction, scale the half-reactions so the electrons cancel: multiply the 3e− half-reaction by 2 and the 2e− half-reaction by 3. Since NO(g) is in the first half-reaction with coefficient 1, after multiplying that half-reaction by 2 its coefficient becomes 2.
